expect:
Top band (5-6): Relevant points are identified, given in detail and logically linked to form a clear account.
Mid band (3-4): Relevant points are identified with attempts at logical linking.
Lower band (1-2): Points are identified and stated simply.
Indicative content:
• Only about 119 years have passed since 1898, far less than the 1600-year half-life, so the activity has barely decreased.
• The notebooks are contaminated — the radioactive material is on the pages, not just irradiating from a distance.
• Alpha radiation has the shortest range in air (a few cm) and is the most ionising — most dangerous at very close range / if inhaled or ingested.
• Beta radiation has a moderate range (~1 m in air) and moderate ionising power — dangerous at short to medium range.
• Gamma radiation has an unlimited range in air and is the least ionising — the dominant hazard at long range.
• Because radium emits all three types (α, β, γ), the notebooks pose a hazard at close range (alpha + beta) and at a distance (gamma).
